inlines.text: A tree grows from 80 cm to 140 cm tall over 5 years.

children.label: a

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Change}&=10-4=6\text{ kg}\\\text{Time}&=8-2=6\text{ months}\\\text{Average rate}&=\frac{6\text{ kg}}{6\text{ months}}=1\text{ kg/month}\end{align*}$$

children.prompt: The temperature was $25^\circ\mathrm{C}$ at 3 pm and $13^\circ\mathrm{C}$ at 6 pm. Find the average decrease in temperature per hour.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Change}&=25-13=12^\circ\mathrm{C}\\\text{Time}&=6-3=3\text{ hours}\\\text{Average rate}&=\frac{12^\circ\mathrm{C}}{3\text{ hours}}=4^\circ\mathrm{C}/\mathrm{hour}\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: Convert these units of time. Only show the operation. You do not need to find the answer.

answer.worked:
Divide by $60$ to convert minutes to hours. Only the operation is required.
$$15\text{ min}=(15\div60)\text{ h}$$

There are $60$ minutes in an hour.
$$\begin{align*}200\text{ min}&=(200\div60)\text{ h}\end{align*}$$

There are $60$ seconds in a minute.
$$\begin{align*}300\text{ s}&=(300\div60)\text{ min}\end{align*}$$

There are $60$ seconds in a minute.
$$\begin{align*}193\text{ min}&=(193\times60)\text{ s}\end{align*}$$

There are $60$ minutes in an hour.
$$\begin{align*}4.5\text{ h}&=(4.5\times60)\text{ min}\end{align*}$$

There are $60$ minutes in an hour.
$$\begin{align*}635\text{ min}&=(635\div60)\text{ h}\end{align*}$$

Convert the hours to minutes, then add the remaining minutes.
$$\begin{align*}4\text{ h }37\text{ min}&=(4\times60+37)\text{ min}\end{align*}$$

Convert the minutes to seconds, then add the remaining seconds.
$$\begin{align*}47\text{ min }12\text{ s}&=(47\times60+12)\text{ s}\end{align*}$$

Convert the days to hours, then add the remaining hours.
$$\begin{align*}5\text{ days }17\text{ h}&=(5\times24+17)\text{ h}\end{align*}$$

There are $24$ hours in a day.
$$\begin{align*}100\text{ h}&=(100\div24)\text{ days}\end{align*}$$

There are $7$ days in a week and $24$ hours in a day.
$$\begin{align*}1\text{ week}&=7\text{ days}\\1\text{ week}&=(7\times24)\text{ h}\end{align*}$$

There are $24$ hours in a day.
$$\begin{align*}10\,000\text{ h}&=(10\,000\div24)\text{ days}\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: Two cars travel toward each other on a 100 km straight stretch of road.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 23 diagram below the prompt, toward the left.
spec.description: Horizontal road with marked endpoints, a centred 100 km label below, and opposing car arrows above. The Car 2 arrow is higher than the Car 1 arrow.
spec.mathematics: The cars start at opposite endpoints of a 100 km road and approach each other at 100 km/h and 80 km/h.
spec.answerVisibility: All diagram labels and arrows are permanent givens; no meeting time or closing speed is supplied.

answer.worked:
Using relative velocity, Car 1 approaches Car 2 at the sum of their speeds.
$$\begin{align*}
s&=100+80\\
s&=180\text{ km/h}\\
t&=\frac{d}{s}\\
t&=\frac{100\text{ km}}{180\text{ km/h}}\\
t&=\frac{5}{9}\text{ h}
\end{align*}$$
Convert to minutes and seconds:
$$\begin{align*}
t&=\frac{5}{9}\times60\text{ min}\\
t&=33\frac{1}{3}\text{ min}\\
t&=33\text{ min }20\text{ s}
\end{align*}$$

The sheets of paper Jenny uses in her photocopier are $21 \text{ cm}$ by $30 \text{ cm}$.
The paper is $80 \text{ gsm}$, which means that one square metre of this paper has a mass of $80 \text{ grams}$.
Jenny has a pile of this paper weighing $25.2 \text{ kg}$.
How many sheets of paper are in the pile?

Circle the correct answer.

(A) 500
(B) 2000
(C) 2500
(D) 5000

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of one sheet}&=0.21\times0.30=0.063\text{ m}^2\\\text{Mass of one sheet}&=0.063\times80=5.04\text{ g}=0.00504\text{ kg}\\\text{Number of sheets}&=25.2\div0.00504=5000\end{align*}$$
There are 5000 sheets (D).

inlines.text: A tap is dripping at the rate of 4 mL per minute.
Which expression shows how many litres this would amount to in one year?

answer.worked:
There are $60\times24\times365$ minutes in one year, and $1000$ mL in one litre.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{4\div1000\text{ L}}{1\div60\div24\div365\text{ year}}&=\frac{4\times60\times24\times365}{1\times1000}\text{ L/year}\\\frac{4\div1000\text{ L}}{1\div60\div24\div365\text{ year}}&=\frac{4\times60\times24\times365}{1000}\text{ L/year}\end{align*}$$
Correct answer: B.

inlines.text: A car had a full tank of 56 L at the start of a 75 km journey.
At the end of the journey, the fuel tank was three quarters full.
What is the fuel consumption rate, in kilometres per litre?
Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Fuel consumed} &= 56-\frac{3}{4}\times56\\\text{Fuel consumed} &= 56-42\\\text{Fuel consumed} &= 14\text{ L}\\\text{Fuel consumption rate} &= \frac{75\text{ km}}{14\text{ L}}\\\text{Fuel consumption rate} &\approx 5.36\text{ km/L}\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: A river is flowing downstream at a rate of 1 km/h.
In still water Portia can swim at a rate of 2 km/h.
Portia dives into the river and swims downstream, then turns around and swims back to the starting point, taking 0.5 hours in total.

answer.short: $0.75\text{ km}=750\text{ m}$ total. The downstream and upstream speeds are $3\text{ km/h}$ and $1\text{ km/h}$; each leg is $0.375\text{ km}$.
answer.worked:
Downstream speed: $2+1=3\text{ km/h}$.

Upstream speed: $2-1=1\text{ km/h}$.

Let the distance swum downstream be $d$ km. The return distance is also $d$ km.

Time downstream + time upstream $=0.5$ h. Using $t=\dfrac{d}{s}$:

$$\begin{align*}\frac{d}{3}+\frac{d}{1}&=0.5\\\frac{4d}{3}&=0.5\\4d&=1.5\\d&=0.375\end{align*}$$

Each leg is $0.375\text{ km}$. Total distance swum:

$$\begin{align*}2d&=2\times0.375\text{ km}\\&=0.75\text{ km}\\&=750\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: Ruth’s tropical fish are breeding at a rate of 8 new fry every 2 days per female fish.
If Ruth has a total of 9 female fish, then how long will it take them to birth a total of 90 new fry?

answer.worked:
For each female fish, $8\div2=4$ new fry per day.

For 9 female fish, $9\times4=36$ new fry per day.

Let $x$ be the time in days. Using equivalent rates and taking reciprocals:

$$\begin{align*}\frac{36}{1}&=\frac{90}{x}\\\frac{1}{36}&=\frac{x}{90}\\90\times\frac{1}{36}&=x\\x&=2.5\end{align*}$$

It takes $2.5$ days.

[Pedagogy audit v2 · Applied automatically · New teaching] Add a short teaching step showing how to find the change from start and end values and then divide by the time.
Worked example: A tree grows from 80 cm to 140 cm tall over 5 years.

1.	Change in height
2.	Time taken
3.	Average rate = change ÷ time
$$\begin{align*}\text{Change}&=140-80=60\text{ cm}\\\text{Time}&=5\text{ years}\\\text{Average rate}&=\frac{60\text{ cm}}{5\text{ years}}\\&=\frac{60\text{ cm}\,\color{#ef6068}{\div5}}{5\text{ years}\,\color{#ef6068}{\div5}}\\&=\frac{12\text{ cm}}{1\text{ year}}\\&=12\text{ cm/year}\end{align*}$$
Guided practice:
Proposed question: Find the average rate of change in each situation.
a) A puppy weighs 4 kg at 2 months old and 10 kg at 8 months old. Find the average increase in mass per month.
b) The temperature was $25^\circ\mathrm{C}$ at 3 pm and $13^\circ\mathrm{C}$ at 6 pm. Find the average decrease in temperature per hour.
Answers: a) $1\text{ kg/month}$; b) $4^\circ\mathrm{C}/\mathrm{hour}$
Applied: Worked example and guided practice added after p4-guided-practice.

entries.description:
A river is flowing downstream at a rate of 1 km/h.
In still water Portia can swim at a rate of 2 km/h.
Portia dives into the river and swims downstream, then turns around and swims back to the starting point, taking 0.5 hours in total.
How far did she swim?

presentation.responseSpace: Open working space beneath the prompt; physical dimensions uncertain.
presentation.requiredInterpretation: The supplied answer identifies the requested distance as the total outward and return distance.

entries.description:
Downstream speed: 2 + 1 = 3 km/h
Upstream speed: 2 − 1 = 1 km/h
Let the distance swum downstream be d km. The return distance is also d km.
Time downstream + Time upstream = 0.5 h
Using t = d/s
d/3 + d/1 = 0.5
4d/3 = 0.5
d = 0.375 km
Total distance swum = 2d = 0.75 km = 750 m

entries.description: Converting Units of Speed

\(\text{speed}=\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}\)
To convert units of speed:
1. Write the rate as a fraction with units.

2. Convert the quantities to the required units.
3. Simplify the fraction using a calculator.

entries.description: Calculating Speed in Distance-Time Graphs

Speed on a distance-time graph
These graphs show distance from the origin. Since speed is distance travelled divided by time taken, we calculate speed from a distance-time graph by doing:
speed = |change in y|/change in x
So, speed is the magnitude of the gradient of the line segment.

entries.description: Related Rates

Related Rates Problems
Usually when working with rates, we only use two units.
Sometimes a question will give a third unit (or more).
To solve these problems:
1. Identify the three quantities in the question.
2. Set up a related rate equation.
\[\frac{\text{Quantity 1}}{\text{Quantity 2}}=\frac{\text{Quantity 1}}{\text{Quantity 3}}\times\frac{\text{Quantity 3}}{\text{Quantity 2}}\]
3. Substitute given information.
The scenario will always give two of the rates.
4. Convert units to be the same, and to the unit wanted by the question.
5. Simplify and solve the equation.
A common application is drip rates for medication, important for doctors and nurses.

4. \[\frac{\text{Drops}}{\text{Time}}=\frac{15\text{ drops}}{1\text{ mL}}\times\frac{1200\text{ mL}}{240\text{ min}}\]
5. \[\frac{\text{Drops}}{\text{Time}}=\frac{75\text{ drops}}{1\text{ min}}\]
75 drops/min
